 Court No. - 65
 Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J.
1 .  List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Prashant Rai, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Shivam Triapathi, learned counsel for the informant, Ms. Ifra Islam, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.0227 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Industrial Area,
District-Prayagraj with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Applicant is the husband of the deceased and he has nothing to do with the said offence.
The trial is moving at snail's pace, as such, there is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial in near future.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 13.12.2023, as such, he is incarcerated for about one year and nine months and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned State Law Officer have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the FIR is prompt and the trial is at its conclusive end as six witnesses have already been examined and the deceased has expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant, as such, he is not entitled for bail.
6. This Court had called for status of trial from the trial court concerned.
As per the status report dated 13.08.2025 received from the trial court concerned, six witnesses have already been examined, as such, the trial is at its conclusive end.

7. The Supreme Court in case of X vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

8. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the promptness of FIR,
trial being at its conclusive end and the deceased expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
9. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.
